requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models' have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The hardware, software libraries, and serving frameworks (PyTorch/HuggingFace, FasterTransformer, CUTLASS INT8 GEMM kernels, NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs) required to run SmoothQuant have been set up.
Compute hardware environment matching the paper (NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs, single-node and multi-GPU serving) is available for accuracy and efficiency experiments.
Code has been implemented that verifies at least one NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU is visible via torch.cuda / nvidia-smi before launching PyTorch benchmarks.

verification.spec: Run a script that calls torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.device_count(), and torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0). Assert at least one visible device whose name matches 'A100' and total_memory >= 79 GiB (80GB variant). Also invoke nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv and assert output contains 'A100' with ~81920 MiB. Fail with a clear error if no A100 80GB is visible before any benchmark runs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports multi-GPU launches on 1/2/4/8 A100 80GB GPUs (as used for OPT-13B through OPT-175B and MT-NLG 530B FasterTransformer runs) via tensor-parallel launchers (e.g., mpirun / torchrun).

verification.spec: Inspect the launch scripts/entrypoints for FasterTransformer benchmarks (e.g., examples for OPT-13B/30B/66B/175B and MT-NLG 530B). Assert that they support tensor-parallel world sizes of 1, 2, 4, and 8 via mpirun or torchrun (e.g., accept a --tensor_para_size or -np argument, or contain explicit configurations for these sizes). Use importlib/ast/grep to confirm the launcher parses TP size and forwards it to the FT runtime; run a dry-run launch with world_size=1 and world_size=2 (if 2 GPUs available) to verify it initializes NCCL without error.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that sets the CUDA compute-capability / architecture flags for A100 (sm_80) when building custom INT8 kernels so that Tensor Core INT8 MMAs are compiled in.

verification.spec: Inspect the CUDA build configuration (setup.py, CMakeLists.txt, or Makefile) used to compile the custom INT8/CUTLASS kernels. Assert that nvcc is invoked with -gencode arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 (or equivalent CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES containing 80). Grep the build logs / compile_commands.json for 'sm_80' or 'compute_80'. Fail if only lower CCs (e.g., sm_70) are present, since Tensor Core INT8 MMA requires sm_80+ on A100.

sub_tasks.requirements: The PyTorch + HuggingFace Transformers proof-of-concept environment used for accuracy evaluation and PyTorch speed/memory measurements is installed.

Code has been implemented that pins/installs a compatible PyTorch version with CUDA support and HuggingFace Transformers capable of loading OPT, BLOOM, GLM-130B, LLaMA, Llama-2, Falcon, Mistral, Mixtral, and OPT-IML checkpoints.

verification.spec: Check that the environment has PyTorch with CUDA (`torch.cuda.is_available()` True) and HuggingFace Transformers importable at a version sufficient to load OPT (AutoModelForCausalLM), BLOOM, LLaMA, Llama-2, Falcon, Mistral, and Mixtral. Attempt `AutoConfig.from_pretrained` (config-only, no weights) on one representative id per family and verify all succeed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that installs and exposes the lm-evaluation-harness (EleutherAI) package so it can be invoked programmatically to evaluate OPT and BLOOM models.

verification.spec: Verify that `lm_eval` (EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) is importable, and that its programmatic API (e.g., `lm_eval.simple_evaluate` or equivalent) can be called with a HuggingFace model to run a trivial task (e.g., a tiny slice of PIQA) and returns a results dict.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that installs / clones the official GLM-130B evaluation repository and makes its evaluation entry points callable for GLM-130B benchmarks.

verification.spec: Verify that the THUDM/GLM-130B evaluation repo is present in the workspace (or installed as a package) and its evaluation entry-point script (e.g., `evaluation/tasks.py` or `evaluate.py`) is importable / executable via a documented CLI. Perform a `--help` invocation and confirm exit code 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Benchmarking and measurement infrastructure for latency and GPU memory (used across Figures 8-9 and Tables 8, 10, 11) is in place.

Code has been implemented that measures end-to-end context-stage latency for a batch of sequences (batch size 4, sequence lengths 128/256/512/1024) using CUDA events and warm-up iterations, matching the protocol used for Figures 8-9.

verification.spec: Import the latency-measurement utility and call it with batch_size=4 and seq_len in {128,256,512,1024} against a small stand-in model. Verify it (a) performs >=3 warm-up iterations, (b) uses `torch.cuda.Event` for timing (or CUDA graph/stream timing), (c) returns a numeric latency in ms, and (d) reports monotonically non-decreasing latency with increasing seq_len on the stand-in model.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that records the aggregated peak GPU memory usage during inference via torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated (or equivalent NVML calls for FasterTransformer) so the memory numbers in Figures 8-9 and Tables 8, 10 can be reproduced.

verification.spec: Run a single inference pass through the memory-measurement wrapper on a small model and confirm it (a) calls `torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats` before the run, (b) calls `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated` (or NVML equivalent for FT) after, and (c) returns a memory value in GB > 0. Inspect returned dict/log.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that measures decoding-stage per-token latency for autoregressive generation at batch sizes 1 and 16 and sequence lengths 512 and 1024, as needed for Table 8.

verification.spec: Invoke the decoding-latency script on a small stand-in causal LM with (batch, seq_len) in {(1,512),(1,1024),(16,512),(16,1024)}. Verify it generates the requested number of new tokens autoregressively, returns per-token latency in ms, and includes warm-up. Verify per-token latency is reported (total_time_ms / new_tokens).

sub_tasks.requirements: All evaluation datasets (LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, OpenBookQA, RTE, COPA, WikiText, MMLU, MNLI, QNLI) and the Pile calibration data are prepared and accessible via the appropriate evaluation harnesses.
The seven zero-shot evaluation tasks used for OPT/BLOOM (LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, OpenBookQA, RTE, COPA) are accessible through the lm-evaluation-harness.
Code has been implemented that loads or configures the lm-evaluation-harness (EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness) to run OPT and BLOOM evaluations.

verification.spec: Verify a config/wrapper script exists that instantiates lm-eval-harness for HuggingFace OPT and BLOOM models. Import the wrapper, run a smoke evaluation on a single task with a tiny model (e.g., opt-125m on 5 PIQA examples), and confirm results are returned.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that registers/uses the LAMBADA task and reports accuracy in a format matching the paper's LAMBADA column.

verification.spec: Run the harness on the LAMBADA task with a tiny model on a limited number of examples and confirm the returned results dict contains a numeric accuracy under a key like `lambada_openai` (or `lambada`). Verify the emitted value is a float in [0,1] and is reported in a format compatible with the paper's LAMBADA column.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, OpenBookQA, RTE, and COPA through the harness and outputs a per-task accuracy for each.

verification.spec: Run the harness with tasks=[hellaswag, piqa, winogrande, openbookqa, rte, copa] on a small model (limit examples) and verify a per-task accuracy is returned for each of the 6 tasks, with values in [0,1].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the average accuracy across the 7 zero-shot tasks (used as the 'Average' column in Table 3 and the WinoGrande/HellaSwag/PIQA/LAMBADA subset in Table 1/4).

verification.spec: Feed a fixed dict of 7 task->accuracy values into the averaging utility and verify it returns the arithmetic mean of the 7 values. Also verify a variant averages only {winogrande, hellaswag, piqa, lambada} for Table 1/4-style aggregation.

sub_tasks.requirements: The WikiText language modeling benchmark is accessible for perplexity evaluation of OPT/BLOOM/LLaMA/Llama-2/Falcon/Mistral/Mixtral.
Code has been implemented that loads the WikiText-2 (raw) dataset for language modeling evaluation.

verification.spec: Call the WikiText-2 loader (e.g., `datasets.load_dataset('wikitext','wikitext-2-raw-v1', split='test')`) and confirm it returns a non-empty dataset with a `text` field. Verify total character/token count matches WikiText-2 test split expectations (>1M characters).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes WikiText perplexity with configurable sequence length (supporting 512 for LLaMA-1 and 2048 for Llama-2/Falcon/Mistral/Mixtral as stated in Tables 6 and 7).

verification.spec: Invoke the WikiText perplexity function on a small HF causal LM (e.g., gpt2) with seq_len=512 and again with seq_len=2048. Verify both invocations succeed, return a positive float PPL, and that changing seq_len is honored (chunking uses the requested length).

sub_tasks.requirements: The GLM-130B evaluation suite (MMLU, MNLI, QNLI, LAMBADA) is set up using GLM-130B's official repository.
Code has been implemented that uses the GLM-130B official evaluation repository (THUDM/GLM-130B) rather than lm-eval-harness for GLM-130B evaluation.

verification.spec: Verify the GLM-130B evaluation code path in the repo invokes the THUDM/GLM-130B repo's evaluation entry point (not lm-eval-harness). Inspect the code (grep/AST) to confirm imports/calls point at the GLM-130B repo modules, and that lm-eval-harness is NOT the driver for GLM-130B tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that evaluates GLM-130B on MMLU, MNLI, QNLI, and LAMBADA and averages the four accuracies (matching the GLM-130B column of Table 4).

verification.spec: Run the GLM-130B evaluation wrapper (with a stubbed/tiny GLM model or a mock) on MMLU, MNLI, QNLI, and LAMBADA and confirm it returns 4 accuracies plus the average of the 4. Verify the average equals mean of the 4 to within numerical precision.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Pile dataset is prepared for calibration of smoothing factors and static quantization step sizes.
Code has been implemented that loads the Pile validation set for calibration sampling.

verification.spec: Call the Pile validation-set loader and confirm it returns an iterable/dataset of text samples with length >= 512 examples (enough for calibration). Verify the returned samples are non-empty strings.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that samples exactly 512 random sentences from the Pile pre-training dataset and uses them (only these) to calibrate smoothing factors and static quantization step sizes once per model.

verification.spec: Invoke the calibration script (e.g., generate_act_scales.py) with defaults on a mock model. Instrument the data loader (via monkeypatch or logging) to count the number of sentences drawn from the Pile validation split. Assert exactly 512 unique samples are consumed, that they are sampled with a fixed seed (reproducible), and that the same calibration is run only once per model to produce a single scales.pt / act_scales.pt file. Also assert the script's CLI default for --num-samples equals 512.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports a separate small Pile validation subset for the alpha grid search described in Section 5.1.

verification.spec: Verify a distinct code path exists for constructing a smaller Pile validation subset used in the alpha grid search (separate from the 512-sample calibration set). Import the subset builder, confirm it accepts a size parameter and a seed, and returns a subset disjoint from (or explicitly configurable relative to) the calibration samples.

sub_tasks.requirements: Evaluation configuration is standardized across quantization variants: the same smoothed+quantized model is applied to all downstream tasks, and relative (not absolute) accuracy change is reported.
Code has been implemented that produces a single calibrated quantized checkpoint per model and evaluates that identical checkpoint on all downstream tasks (no per-task recalibration).

verification.spec: Trace the pipeline: run calibration once on a small model to produce a single quantized checkpoint file, then run 2 different downstream task evaluations pointing at that same checkpoint path. Verify (a) only one calibration invocation occurs, (b) both evaluations load an identical checkpoint hash, and (c) no recalibration is triggered per-task.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that logs FP16-baseline vs. quantized accuracy/perplexity side-by-side for each dataset so the reported delta (relative change) can be reproduced.

verification.spec: Run the reporting utility with (fp16_result, quantized_result) pairs on 2 datasets for a tiny model. Verify the output log/CSV/JSON contains both FP16 and quantized scores side-by-side per dataset AND explicitly reports the delta (quantized - fp16) or relative change.

sub_tasks.requirements: For GLM-130B calibration, code has been implemented that clips the top 2% tokens when collecting static quantization step-size statistics, following Wei et al. (2022) as specified in Section 5.2.

verification.spec: Run the GLM-130B calibration path (or the code branch selected when model_name contains 'glm') on a small stand-in model with recorded activation tensors. Instrument the step-size collection routine to log the fraction of tokens discarded before computing max(|X|). Assert that the top 2% of token activations by magnitude are clipped/removed prior to computing the static step size (i.e., the routine uses a quantile of 0.98 rather than the raw max). Verify this branch is only taken for GLM-130B configs, not OPT/BLOOM.

sub_tasks.requirements: The integer uniform quantization primitives (per-tensor, per-token, per-channel, group-wise; static and dynamic) described in Section 2 are implemented consistent with Equation 1 and Figure 3.
The core uniform symmetric integer quantizer from Equation 1 is implemented.

Code has been implemented that provides a uniform quantization function taking an FP tensor and returning INT8 values (or their dequantized floats) along with the step size Delta, following X_bar = round(X/Delta) with Delta = max(|X|)/(2^(N-1)-1) for N=8.

verification.spec: Import the project's quantize function. Feed X = torch.tensor([-3.2, -1.0, 0.0, 0.5, 2.7]). Assert returned Delta = max(|X|) / 127 = 3.2/127 ≈ 0.0252, and returned int8 tensor equals round(X/Delta) clipped to [-127,127]: [-127, -40, 0, 20, 107] (allow off-by-one for rounding-half-to-even). Also verify dequantize(quantize(X)) approximates X with max error <= Delta. Repeat with a 2D tensor to confirm per-tensor behavior.

sub_tasks.requirements: The quantizer uses maximum absolute value (max(|X|)) to compute Delta so that outliers are preserved, and clamps outputs to the signed INT8 range [-127, 127] with round-to-nearest ties.

verification.spec: Feed the quantizer a tensor containing an extreme outlier, e.g., X = torch.tensor([0.1, 0.2, -0.1, 100.0]). Assert Delta is derived from max(|X|)=100 (not from a clipped/percentile value), that the outlier maps to +127 (i.e., preserved rather than saturated below 127), that all outputs lie in [-127, 127] inclusive, and that rounding uses round-half-to-nearest-even (verify by checking X=0.5*Delta rounds to 0 with banker's rounding or to 1 with half-up — accept either but assert consistency across values).

sub_tasks.requirements: Round-trip quantize-then-dequantize of a random FP16 tensor with the implemented primitive produces values within one Delta of the original tensor (unit-test behavioral check).

verification.spec: Generate a random FP16 tensor X (shape 128x128, uniform in [-10,10]). Quantize with the implemented symmetric INT8 quantizer to obtain X_int and Delta, then dequantize as X_hat = X_int.float()*Delta. Assert torch.max(torch.abs(X - X_hat)) <= Delta + 1e-5 (i.e., within one Delta everywhere).

sub_tasks.requirements: Granularity schemes (per-tensor, per-token, per-channel, group-wise) from Figure 3 are implemented with correct axis conventions.
Code has been implemented for per-tensor quantization that computes a single scalar Delta for the entire tensor/matrix.

verification.spec: Call the per-tensor quantizer on a 2D FP16 tensor of shape [T=64, C=32] and assert the returned Delta is a scalar (shape () or (1,)) equal to max(|X|)/(2^(N-1)-1) with N=8. Also verify the quantized tensor is int8 dtype and torch.all(torch.abs(x_int) <= 127).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for per-token activation quantization that produces a Delta vector of shape [T, 1] (one step size per token along the outer dimension T), matching Figure 3(b).

verification.spec: Call the per-token activation quantizer on a tensor X of shape [T=16, C=64]. Assert the returned Delta has shape (16, 1) and Delta[t,0] == max(|X[t,:]|)/127 for each row t. Verify quantized tensor is int8, all values in [-127, 127].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for per-channel weight quantization that produces a Delta vector of shape [1, C_o] along the output-channel dimension, matching Figure 3(b).

verification.spec: Call the per-channel weight quantizer on W of shape [C_i=32, C_o=48]. Assert returned Delta has shape (1, 48) and Delta[0,c] == max(|W[:,c]|)/127. Verify quantized W is int8 within [-127,127].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a simulated per-channel activation quantization along the input-channel dimension C_i (for accuracy analysis / motivation experiments only, not for GEMM kernels).

verification.spec: Call the simulated per-channel-along-C_i activation quantizer on X of shape [T=16, C_i=32]. Assert the Delta has shape (1, 32) computed per input channel (Delta[0,c]==max(|X[:,c]|)/127), and that fake_quant(X) matches X within one Delta_c per column. Confirm this path is flagged as simulation-only (not exposed to INT8 GEMM).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for group-wise weight quantization that partitions channels into groups of configurable size and computes one Delta per group (as used by ZeroQuant-style baselines).

verification.spec: Call the group-wise weight quantizer on W of shape [C_i=64, C_o=64] with group_size=16. Assert the returned Delta has shape (4, C_o) or equivalent (one Delta per group of 16 input channels per output channel), and that quantized values in each group use the group's max-abs. Also test group_size=32 and 128 as configurable options.

sub_tasks.requirements: The granularity API enforces that only outer-dimension scaling (token dim T for activations, output channel dim C_o for weights) is used when producing INT8 tensors intended for INT8 GEMM kernels; inner-dimension (C_i) scaling is only allowed in the simulated per-channel-activation path.

verification.spec: Attempt to call the INT8-GEMM-facing quantize API with an activation scale axis along C_i (inner dim): expect a ValueError/assertion. Then call with activation scaling along T (outer): expect success. Same for weight: scaling along C_o succeeds, along C_i raises. The simulated-only path (previous leaf) must be reachable via a separate flag (e.g., simulate=True) and must not be reachable from the GEMM path.

sub_tasks.requirements: Static vs dynamic quantization modes are implemented consistent with Section 2.
Code has been implemented for dynamic quantization that computes Delta from the runtime statistics (max(|X|)) of each input tensor on the fly during inference.

verification.spec: Instantiate the dynamic quantizer (e.g., W8A8Linear with act_quant='per_token_dynamic' or 'per_tensor_dynamic'). Run two forward passes with inputs of very different magnitudes (X1 in [-1,1], X2 in [-100,100]). Instrument the internal Delta and assert Delta_2 ≈ 100 * Delta_1 (i.e., recomputed from current input's max abs value each call, not cached across calls). Verify no calibration file / stored scale is read at inference time for this mode.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for static quantization that pre-computes and stores Delta values offline using a calibration pass over a set of calibration samples, and reuses those fixed step sizes at inference time.

verification.spec: (1) Run the calibration pass on a small dataset to produce a per-tensor static Delta stored on the module (e.g., register_buffer('act_scale', ...)). (2) Perform two forward passes with inputs of very different magnitudes; instrument the quantizer and assert Delta is identical across both calls and equals the calibrated value (not re-derived from current input). (3) Verify state_dict save/load preserves the Delta buffer. (4) Verify the calibration entrypoint writes a scales file to disk that inference reuses.

sub_tasks.requirements: A calibration routine is provided that runs the FP model on a specified number of calibration sentences (default 512 from Pile) and records per-tensor/per-token/per-channel activation max-abs statistics used to populate static Deltas.

verification.spec: Run the calibration routine on OPT-125M with num_samples=512 sentences sampled from the Pile validation set. Assert it registers forward hooks on all target linear inputs, accumulates per-tensor / per-token / per-channel max-abs statistics, and populates static Delta tables for every target module (dict keyed by module name). Confirm changing num_samples to 8 yields a smaller-but-nonzero stat dictionary (routine is parameterized).

sub_tasks.requirements: The static calibration path supports an optional top-k percentile clipping option (e.g., clipping the top 2% of tokens when calibrating step sizes, as used for GLM-130B following Wei et al. 2022).

verification.spec: Invoke calibration with clip_top_percentile=0.02 on a synthetic activation stream containing known outliers in the top 2% of tokens. Assert the resulting static Delta is strictly smaller than the un-clipped Delta (max-abs) and equals the 98th-percentile-based max. Also verify the option defaults to no clipping and can be turned on selectively for GLM-130B in the config.

sub_tasks.requirements: Mathematical-equivalence checks are provided to verify the primitives.

A unit test demonstrates that applying per-token activation quantization together with per-channel weight quantization and then rescaling by (Delta_X outer Delta_W) after INT8 matmul reproduces the FP matmul result Y = X @ W within quantization error tolerance, matching the outer-dimension scaling formula in Section 3.

verification.spec: Take random X of shape [T=32, C_i=64] and W of shape [C_i=64, C_o=48] in FP16. Compute Y_fp = X @ W. Quantize X per-token (Delta_X shape [T,1]) and W per-channel (Delta_W shape [1,C_o]) to int8; compute Y_int = X_int.int() @ W_int.int(); then Y_hat = Y_int.float() * Delta_X * Delta_W. Assert torch.max(torch.abs(Y_fp - Y_hat)) / torch.max(torch.abs(Y_fp)) < 0.05 (5% relative error, within quantization tolerance) and shapes match [T, C_o].

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that simulated per-channel activation quantization on OPT-6.7B for a single linear layer (or a lightweight proxy) yields substantially smaller reconstruction error than per-tensor and per-token quantization on the same activation tensor, reproducing the qualitative Table 1 trend.

verification.spec: Load OPT-6.7B, extract input activations to a decoder-layer linear (e.g., fc1) over ~128 tokens of calibration text, then simulate INT8 fake-quantization under three schemes: per-tensor (single absmax scale), per-token (per-row absmax), per-channel (per-input-channel absmax). Compute MSE between quantized-dequantized activations and original FP16 activations. Assert MSE(per-channel) < MSE(per-token) and MSE(per-channel) < MSE(per-tensor) by at least 5x, matching the Table 1 qualitative trend.

sub_tasks.requirements: The observations that motivate SmoothQuant — outliers persist in fixed channels, per-channel activation quantization preserves accuracy while per-tensor/per-token do not (Table 1) — are reproduced.
Activation and weight statistics are collected from a linear layer of an OPT model to characterize the outlier patterns.

Code has been implemented to hook a linear layer of an OPT model (e.g., OPT-13B) and record the input activation tensor and weight tensor over a batch of calibration tokens from a text corpus (e.g., Pile validation subset).

verification.spec: Import the calibration hook utility; instantiate an OPT model (e.g., facebook/opt-125m as a lightweight proxy), register a forward hook on a chosen decoder linear layer, run a forward pass over a small text batch, and assert that the hook has captured (a) the input activation tensor with shape [tokens, in_features] and (b) the weight tensor with shape [out_features, in_features], both as torch tensors.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute per-channel maximum absolute magnitudes across tokens for the activation tensor, and per-output-channel maximum magnitudes for the weight tensor, storing them as 1-D arrays over the input-channel and output-channel dimensions respectively.

verification.spec: Call the utility that, given an activation tensor of shape [T, Ci] and a weight of shape [Co, Ci], returns per-channel activation absmax (1-D array of length Ci) and per-output-channel weight absmax (1-D array of length Co). Verify shapes, positivity, and that values equal manually computed torch.abs(...).amax over the correct dimensions.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to visualize (as 3-D surface plots or heatmaps over tokens x channels) the activation and weight magnitudes, matching the layout of Figure 4 with tokens on one axis and channels on the other.

verification.spec: Invoke the visualization utility on a captured (activation, weight) pair; assert it produces two image files (e.g., PNG) whose axes correspond to tokens and channels (activation) and to in-channels and out-channels (weight), similar to Figure 4. Check files exist and are non-empty; if the API returns matplotlib figures, assert the axes labels/dimensions match tokens x channels.

sub_tasks.requirements: The three motivating observations about activation outliers are verified quantitatively.

The analysis confirms observation (1): the weight distribution of a linear layer in an OPT model is uniform/flat, with the ratio between max absolute weight and mean absolute weight remaining within a small constant (e.g., less than ~10x), and no isolated outlier channels dominate.

verification.spec: Load a pretrained OPT model (e.g., facebook/opt-1.3b or opt-13b). For each nn.Linear layer in the decoder blocks, compute max(|W|) / mean(|W|) and the per-output-channel max-to-median ratio. Assert (a) global max/mean ratio is < 20 for at least 90% of linear layers (flat/uniform), and (b) no single output channel has max magnitude > 10x the median channel's max, confirming the weight distribution is flat with no isolated outlier channels (matching Figure 4 observation 3).

sub_tasks.requirements: The analysis confirms observation (2): a small fraction of activation channels have magnitudes roughly ~100x larger than most other channels, i.e., max activation magnitude / median channel magnitude is on the order of 100 for at least one linear layer.

verification.spec: Load OPT-13B in FP16, run a forward pass on a small batch of calibration text through the model, and hook the input activations to a specific linear layer known to have outliers (e.g., the self-attention or FFN input in a mid-network layer). Compute per-channel max absolute magnitudes across all tokens. Verify that max(channel_max) / median(channel_max) >= 50 (loosely bracketing the ~100x claim). Report the ratio.

sub_tasks.requirements: The analysis confirms observation (3): outlier channels are persistent across tokens — the set of top-k largest-magnitude channels (e.g., top 1%) computed per token has high overlap (Jaccard or hit rate approaching 1) with the globally top-k channels, demonstrating outliers stay in fixed channel indices.

verification.spec: Load OPT-13B in FP16, capture input activations to a linear layer over a batch of calibration tokens. For each token, identify the top-1% channels by absolute magnitude, and compute the global top-1% channels using the max magnitude aggregated across tokens. Verify that the mean per-token Jaccard overlap (or hit rate) between per-token top-1% channels and global top-1% channels is >= 0.7, evidencing that outlier channels are persistent across tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: The analysis computes and reports the variance of magnitudes across channels for a fixed token versus the variance across tokens for a fixed channel, showing across-channel variance >> across-token (within-channel) variance for outlier channels.

verification.spec: On a captured OPT-13B (or smaller OPT proxy) activation tensor from a linear layer known to have outlier channels, compute (a) variance of magnitudes across channels for each token (then average), (b) variance across tokens for each channel (then average over outlier channels defined as top-1% by absmax). Assert (a) >> (b) (ratio > 10x), reproducing the paper's observation that outlier channels persist across tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: The SmoothQuant transformation — per-channel smoothing factor s with migration strength alpha (Equation 4), offline fusion into preceding layers, application to attention and FFN linear layers, and per-block precision mapping (Figure 6) — is correctly implemented.
Calibration pipeline to collect per-input-channel activation statistics is implemented.

Code has been implemented to run a forward-pass calibration hook over a user-specified set of linear layers, accumulating the per-input-channel absolute maxima of the activations feeding each hooked layer.

verification.spec: Instantiate a small OPT model, call the calibration utility with a list of target linear-layer names and a small text corpus. Assert the returned mapping contains, for each named layer, a 1-D tensor of length in_features whose values equal the manual running-max of |activation| across the calibration tokens (compare to a reference computation on the same inputs).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so calibration uses 512 random sentences drawn from the Pile pre-training corpus by default, with configurable sample count and dataset path.

verification.spec: Call the calibration function with default arguments and inspect the sampler: assert num_samples default == 512, dataset defaults to Pile (or configurable path/HF dataset id containing 'pile'), and that both num_samples and dataset_path are exposed as function/CLI arguments overridable by the user.

sub_tasks.requirements: Calibration is performed once per model, producing a single set of smoothing factors and (for static quantization) step sizes that are reused across all downstream evaluation tasks.

verification.spec: Run the end-to-end pipeline: (1) calibrate once on a small model to produce smoothing factors + static step sizes saved to disk; (2) load those artifacts and evaluate on two different downstream tasks (e.g., lambada and piqa) without recalibrating. Assert the same artifact hash/values are used for both evaluations and the calibration function is not invoked a second time.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to optionally clip the top 2% of tokens when calibrating static quantization step sizes, and this option is enabled for GLM-130B calibration (following Wei et al., 2022).

verification.spec: Call the static-quantization calibration with clip_top_tokens_pct=0.02 on a synthetic activation tensor containing a known heavy tail; verify that the resulting scale equals the 98th-percentile absmax (not the true max). Additionally verify the GLM-130B config/preset enables this clipping option by default (clip=0.02).

sub_tasks.requirements: The smoothing-factor formula (Equation 4) with configurable migration strength alpha is correctly implemented.
Code has been implemented that, given per-channel activation absolute maxima |X_j| and weight absolute maxima |W_j|, computes s_j = max(|X_j|)^alpha / max(|W_j|)^(1-alpha) as in Equation 4.

verification.spec: Import the smoothing-factor function (e.g., smooth_lm or compute_smoothing_scale). Provide per-channel act_max = torch.tensor([1.0, 10.0, 100.0]) and weight_max = torch.tensor([1.0, 1.0, 1.0]) with alpha=0.5. Assert the returned s equals [1.0^0.5/1.0^0.5, 10.0^0.5/1.0^0.5, 100.0^0.5/1.0^0.5] = [1.0, 3.1623, 10.0] within 1e-5. Repeat with alpha=0.75 and non-unit weight_max to verify the full Equation 4 formula. Also assert numerical stability: s is clamped to avoid divide-by-zero when act_max or weight_max contain zeros.

sub_tasks.requirements: The smoothing implementation exposes the migration strength alpha as a configurable hyperparameter and defaults it to 0.5 for OPT/BLOOM-family models.

verification.spec: Inspect the smoothing API (function/CLI signature) via inspect.signature or argparse introspection. Assert that alpha is an explicit parameter (not hardcoded) and that its default value is 0.5. Grep the OPT/BLOOM model configs / examples to confirm they invoke smoothing with alpha=0.5 (no override). Also assert alpha can be overridden per-model (e.g., 0.75 for GLM-130B, 0.85 for Llama-2).

sub_tasks.requirements: Weight max computation for s_j uses the per-input-channel absolute maximum across output channels of the target weight matrix, consistent with the per-channel formulation.

verification.spec: Given a weight tensor W of shape [Co, Ci], call the smoothing-scale computation and inspect the weight-side statistic: assert it equals torch.abs(W).amax(dim=0), producing a 1-D array of length Ci (per-input-channel absmax across output channels), matching the formulation s_j = max(|W_j|).

sub_tasks.requirements: Numerical safeguards (e.g., clamping the denominator |W_j|^(1-alpha) away from zero) are implemented so that s contains no NaNs/Infs on real activation and weight tensors.

verification.spec: Construct pathological inputs (weight column with all zeros, activation channel with zero max, alpha=0.5) and call the smoothing-scale computation. Assert the returned s tensor contains no NaN and no Inf values (torch.isfinite(s).all()) and s > 0 everywhere.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies mathematical equivalence: for a random linear layer Y=X·W, applying X_hat = X·diag(s)^-1 and W_hat = diag(s)·W yields Y' = X_hat·W_hat equal to the original Y within float32 tolerance (max abs diff < 1e-4).

verification.spec: In a pytest test: set torch.manual_seed(0); create X of shape (8, 64) and W of shape (64, 32) in float32; sample s in float32 with values in [0.1, 10.0] of shape (64,). Compute Y_ref = X @ W. Compute X_hat = X / s (broadcast on last dim) and W_hat = s.unsqueeze(1) * W. Compute Y_new = X_hat @ W_hat. Assert (Y_new - Y_ref).abs().max() < 1e-4. This confirms the mathematical equivalence property before any quantization is applied.

sub_tasks.requirements: Offline fusion of the smoothing factor s into the preceding layer's parameters is correctly implemented.
Code has been implemented to fuse s^-1 into the weight and bias of a preceding LayerNorm (dividing the LN gamma and beta by s element-wise) so that its output is pre-smoothed at runtime.

verification.spec: Build a torch nn.LayerNorm(64) with random gamma and beta, and a smoothing vector s of shape (64,) with random positive values. Call the project's fuse function (e.g., smooth_ln_fcs or fuse_ln). Assert that ln.weight.data has been divided by s element-wise, ln.bias.data has been divided by s element-wise, and the fused LN's output on a random input equals the original LN's output divided by s within 1e-5. Ensure the fusion is done offline (no runtime hooks) and modifies the module in-place.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to fuse s^-1 into the output columns of a preceding linear layer (dividing the corresponding weight columns and bias entries by s) when the smoothed activation is produced by a Linear rather than a LayerNorm.

verification.spec: Build a tiny two-linear model (Linear1 -> Linear2). Compute a smoothing vector s and call the fusion utility with prev=Linear1, next=Linear2. Assert Linear1.weight is divided by s along its output rows and Linear1.bias is divided by s, while Linear2.weight is multiplied by s along its input columns. Verify that forward outputs on random inputs match the pre-fusion model within 1e-4 (mathematical equivalence).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to correspondingly scale the target linear layer's weights by diag(s) along the input-channel dimension, so that the fused model is numerically equivalent to the original.

verification.spec: Build an nn.Linear(64, 32) with random FP32 weight; call the smoothing fusion helper with vector s of shape (64,). Assert linear.weight has been multiplied by s along the input-channel dim (i.e., new_weight[:, j] == old_weight[:, j] * s[j] for all j) within 1e-6. Verify shape is preserved and bias (if present) is unchanged. Then confirm linear(x/s) == old_linear(x) within 1e-5 for random x.

sub_tasks.requirements: For inputs arriving through a residual add, code has been implemented to insert an extra scaling on the residual branch so the fused transformation remains mathematically equivalent (following Wei et al., 2022).

verification.spec: Construct a mini-block with a residual add feeding a linear whose input we wish to smooth. Apply the smoothing utility; verify an explicit scaling of 1/s is inserted on the residual branch such that the block's output on random FP16 input matches the unsmoothed reference within 1e-4.

sub_tasks.requirements: An end-to-end equivalence test runs a full transformer block on random input before and after offline smoothing fusion (no quantization) and asserts outputs match within FP16 numerical tolerance.

verification.spec: Load a small pretrained transformer block (e.g., one OPT-125M decoder layer) in FP16 on GPU. Feed a fixed random hidden state x (batch=2, seq=32, hidden=768) through the original block to get y_ref. Apply the offline smoothing fusion (compute act scales on x, fuse into LN + linear) WITHOUT quantization. Feed the same x through the fused block to get y_fused. Assert (y_ref - y_fused).abs().max() / y_ref.abs().max() < 1e-2 (FP16 tolerance). Confirms fusion is numerically equivalent.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-block precision mapping matches Figure 6.
All linear layers (Q/K/V projections, attention output projection, FC1, FC2) use INT8 arithmetic on both weights and inputs at inference time.

verification.spec: After converting a small OPT to the SmoothQuant INT8 inference model, walk every decoder block and verify that q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, out_proj, fc1, fc2 have been replaced by INT8 linear modules (weights stored as int8, activation quantizer present). Standard nn.Linear instances must not remain inside these positions.

sub_tasks.requirements: Both batched matrix multiplications inside the self-attention (Q·K^T and Attn·V) execute with INT8 inputs, per Figure 6.

verification.spec: Inspect the SmoothQuant self-attention module: verify that both the Q*K^T batched matmul and the Attn*V batched matmul are dispatched via INT8 BMM kernels (e.g., call sites reference an int8_bmm / CUTLASS INT8 GEMM wrapper, and inputs are quantized to torch.int8 immediately before the matmul).

sub_tasks.requirements: Softmax, LayerNorm, ReLU/GELU and other element-wise operations remain in FP16, matching the Figure 6 precision map.

verification.spec: Run a forward pass through a SmoothQuant OPT block with hooks on Softmax, LayerNorm, and GELU/ReLU: assert every one of these ops receives and returns torch.float16 (or float32) tensors, never int8. Also confirm no INT8 quantizer is installed on these modules.

sub_tasks.requirements: The residual additions in each transformer block are performed in FP16 after dequantizing linear/BMM outputs, as depicted in Figure 6.

verification.spec: Hook the residual-add operations in a SmoothQuant decoder layer during forward. Assert both operands and the output of each residual add are FP16 tensors (dequantized after the preceding linear/BMM). Confirm no int8 tensor enters the residual pathway.

sub_tasks.requirements: End-to-end validation of the SmoothQuant transformation.

After applying SmoothQuant offline, the per-input-channel activation magnitude range of a target linear layer (e.g., OPT-13B attention input) is dramatically compressed relative to the unsmoothed activations, reproducing the qualitative pattern shown in Figure 4.

verification.spec: Capture the input activations to a decoder attention linear (e.g., q_proj in layer 12) of OPT-13B before and after applying SmoothQuant offline transformation. Compute per-input-channel absmax vectors; report the ratio max(absmax_before)/max(absmax_after). Expect a large compression: ratio >= 10x (Figure 4 shows outlier magnitudes going from >70 to close to 1 after smoothing).

sub_tasks.requirements: A regression test confirms that running the SmoothQuant-transformed model in FP16 (no quantization applied yet) matches the original FP16 model outputs to within numerical tolerance on a batch of calibration inputs, verifying mathematical equivalence of the smoothing+fusion step.

verification.spec: Load a small transformer model (e.g., OPT-125M), apply SmoothQuant smoothing+fusion but keep weights/activations in FP16 (skip quantization). Run a batch of calibration inputs through both the original and smoothed FP16 models and compare final logits: max absolute difference should be < 1e-3 and cosine similarity > 0.9999, confirming mathematical equivalence of the smoothing transform.

sub_tasks.requirements: The three SmoothQuant efficiency configurations (O1/O2/O3) and the calibration procedure using 512 Pile sentences are implemented as described in Table 2 and Section 5.1.
The three SmoothQuant quantization efficiency levels O1, O2, and O3 are implemented with the correct weight/activation granularity and static/dynamic modes per Table 2.
SmoothQuant-O1 configuration is implemented: per-tensor INT8 weight quantization combined with per-token dynamic INT8 activation quantization for all quantized linear layers.

verification.spec: Instantiate a small transformer, configure it with SmoothQuant-O1, and verify by inspection of quantizer objects and by feeding two different input batches: (a) weight scales are single scalars per linear layer (per-tensor), (b) activation scales have shape [T,1] recomputed per input (per-token dynamic), and (c) scales differ between different input batches for activations but not for weights.

sub_tasks.requirements: SmoothQuant-O2 configuration is implemented: per-tensor INT8 weight quantization combined with per-tensor dynamic INT8 activation quantization (activation scale computed at runtime from the current tensor's max).

verification.spec: Instantiate a small transformer with SmoothQuant-O2 config; feed two different input batches to a quantized linear layer. Assert: weight scale is a single scalar per layer, activation scale is a single scalar per layer computed at runtime, and the activation scale changes between different inputs (dynamic behavior).

sub_tasks.requirements: SmoothQuant-O3 configuration is implemented: per-tensor INT8 weight quantization combined with per-tensor static INT8 activation quantization using calibration-derived fixed activation scales at inference time (no runtime scale computation).

verification.spec: Instantiate a small transformer with SmoothQuant-O3 after running calibration; feed two different input batches to a quantized linear layer. Assert: weight scale is a scalar per layer, activation scale is a scalar per layer, and the activation scale is IDENTICAL across the two different input batches (static). Also assert that no max-reduction op appears in the forward path via tracing or by monkey-patching torch.max.

sub_tasks.requirements: A single configuration switch (e.g., O1/O2/O3 flag) selects the appropriate weight granularity, activation granularity, and static-vs-dynamic mode for all linear layers and BMMs in a model without requiring code edits.

verification.spec: From a single Python entry point, call the quantization API three times with only the flag/argument differing (e.g., quant_level='O1', 'O2', 'O3') on the same base model. Verify each returns a working quantized model whose per-layer quantizer types match the Table 2 O1/O2/O3 spec, without any additional code changes.

sub_tasks.requirements: The calibration procedure that estimates smoothing factors and static activation quantization step sizes from 512 Pile sentences is implemented per Section 5.1.
Code has been implemented to sample 512 random sentences from the Pile pre-training dataset for calibration, used for both smoothing factor estimation and static quantization step-size collection.

verification.spec: Invoke the calibration data loading function; verify it returns exactly 512 samples sourced from the Pile dataset (e.g., by inspecting dataset name/URL in the loader). Verify random sampling is deterministic given a seed and produces 512 distinct sentences.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to register activation hooks on all target linear-layer inputs (and BMM operands) during a calibration forward pass and to record the per-channel absolute-maximum statistics needed for computing smoothing factors s.

verification.spec: Register the calibration hooks on a small OPT model, run one forward pass on a batch, and verify: (a) hooks are attached to every target linear layer input and BMM operand, (b) recorded statistics have shape [C_i] (per-channel), and (c) values equal the true per-channel abs-max of the recorded inputs (compared against a manual computation).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to collect per-tensor activation absolute-maximum statistics over the 512 calibration sentences to derive the static per-tensor activation quantization step sizes used in the O3 configuration.

verification.spec: Run the per-tensor activation calibration procedure on 512 Pile sentences with a small OPT model. Verify a single scalar abs-max is stored per activation tensor, and that this scalar equals the max over all tokens and channels across the 512 samples (verified against a reference computation on a small subset).

sub_tasks.requirements: Calibration is performed once per model, and the resulting smoothing factors and static activation scales are serialized (e.g., saved to disk) and reused across all downstream evaluation tasks without recalibration.

verification.spec: Run calibration on a small model, serialize smoothing factors and activation scales to disk. Then load them in a fresh Python process and verify: (a) file exists and contains all expected tensors, (b) loading + applying to two different evaluation tasks does not re-invoke the calibration procedure (monitor by adding a counter/assert in the calibration function), and (c) evaluation runs succeed on multiple tasks with the same loaded artifacts.

sub_tasks.requirements: For GLM-130B calibration, top-2% activation tokens are clipped when computing static quantization step sizes (following Wei et al. 2022), while other models use the unclipped absolute maximum.

verification.spec: Run the static activation calibration path with model_name='glm-130b' style flag using a small proxy model; verify the code applies top-2% token clipping (e.g., inspect that the abs-max collector uses torch.quantile(x_abs, 0.98) or a top-k excluding top 2% before taking max). Also verify that when a different model name is used, no clipping is applied (raw max).

sub_tasks.requirements: The three O1/O2/O3 configurations behave correctly at inference time and produce the expected efficiency ordering.

At inference in O1/O2 mode, activation quantization scales are computed dynamically from the current input tensor (per-token for O1, per-tensor for O2); in O3 mode the pre-calibrated static scales are used and no runtime max reduction occurs on activations.

verification.spec: For each of O1, O2, O3, run inference on two distinct input batches through a quantized linear layer. Verify: (O1) activation scale has shape [T,1] and differs between batches; (O2) scale is scalar and differs between batches; (O3) scale is scalar and IDENTICAL between batches. Also profile O3 to confirm no runtime torch.max/torch.amax is called on activations in the forward path (e.g., by patching torch.max with a counter).

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured per-layer or end-to-end latency satisfies O1 > O2 > O3 (i.e., O3 is fastest and O1 is slowest among the three) on OPT-13B/OPT-30B, matching the efficiency ordering claimed in Table 2 and Table 11.

verification.spec: Benchmark end-to-end latency for OPT-13B under SmoothQuant O1, O2, and O3 with batch size 4 and sequence length 512 on a single H100 GPU. Warm up 3 iterations then time 20 iterations. Verify latency(O3) < latency(O2) < latency(O1); measure the value latency(O1)/latency(O3) (paper reports 243.3/223.1 ≈ 1.09 for OPT-13B seq 512).

sub_tasks.requirements: The comparison baselines (W8A8 naive, ZeroQuant, LLM.int8(), Outlier Suppression) are implemented per Table 2 for accuracy and latency comparisons.
The W8A8 naive baseline is implemented with per-tensor static/dynamic quantization for both weights and activations, matching Table 2's row 'W8A8: per-tensor weight, per-tensor dynamic activation'.

Code has been implemented that provides a W8A8 naive quantization routine performing per-tensor symmetric INT8 quantization on the weight tensor of each linear layer using max-absolute value to compute the scale.

verification.spec: Call the W8A8 naive weight quantizer on a known FP16 weight tensor; verify the returned dequantized tensor equals round(W/scale)*scale where scale = W.abs().max()/127 (single scalar per matrix). Verify shape preservation and INT8 range compliance ([-128,127]).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that applies per-tensor dynamic INT8 activation quantization for the W8A8 naive baseline, computing the quantization scale at runtime from the current activation tensor's max-absolute value.

verification.spec: Feed two different activation tensors into the W8A8-naive activation quantizer; verify that (a) the scale is a single scalar equal to X.abs().max()/127, (b) it is recomputed per input (differs across the two inputs), and (c) quantized values lie in [-128, 127] and dequantize to round(X/scale)*scale.

sub_tasks.requirements: The naive W8A8 baseline substantially degrades accuracy on OPT-175B, reproducing the average accuracy across the 7 zero-shot tasks reported in Table 3 (~35.5%) versus FP16 (~66.9%).

verification.spec: Apply naive W8A8 quantization to OPT-175B and evaluate the 7 zero-shot tasks (LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, OpenBookQA, RTE, COPA) using lm-eval-harness. Report the average accuracy across the 7 tasks; expected ~35.5% (paper Table 3), significantly below FP16 ~66.9%.

sub_tasks.requirements: The ZeroQuant baseline is implemented with group-wise weight quantization and per-token dynamic activation quantization as described in Yao et al. 2022 and Table 2.
Code has been implemented that performs group-wise INT8 weight quantization for the ZeroQuant baseline, partitioning each weight matrix's input channels into groups and using one scale per group.

verification.spec: Call the ZeroQuant group-wise weight quantizer with group_size=128 on a weight matrix of shape [C_i, C_o]. Verify: (a) number of stored scales equals ceil(C_i/128)*C_o (one per (group, output channel)), (b) each group's scale equals that group's abs-max divided by 127, and (c) dequantized values match a reference implementation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that performs per-token dynamic INT8 activation quantization for ZeroQuant, computing a separate scale per token (row of the activation matrix) at runtime.

verification.spec: Feed an activation tensor of shape [T, C] through the ZeroQuant per-token activation quantizer. Verify: (a) the scale tensor has shape [T, 1], (b) each row's scale equals X[t].abs().max()/127, and (c) scales are recomputed per input batch (dynamic).

sub_tasks.requirements: The ZeroQuant baseline supports the ablation variant used in Table 3 (footnote), where self-attention input activations are kept in FP16 while the remainder are quantized to INT8.

verification.spec: Enable the ZeroQuant variant flag that keeps self-attention input activations in FP16. Inspect the wrapped model: verify (a) the q/k/v projection input quantizers are bypassed (activations remain FP16), and (b) all other linear layers (out proj, FFN) still apply INT8 activation quantization. A forward pass runs without errors and produces different outputs than the fully-quantized variant.

sub_tasks.requirements: The ZeroQuant baseline reproduces the accuracy degradation on OPT-175B reported in Table 3 (~35.8% average across the 7 zero-shot tasks, WikiText PPL ~84648).

verification.spec: Apply ZeroQuant (group-wise weight + per-token dynamic activation INT8) to OPT-175B and evaluate on the 7 zero-shot tasks using lm-eval-harness. Report the average accuracy; expected ~35.8% (paper Table 3), indicating substantial degradation from FP16.

sub_tasks.requirements: The LLM.int8() baseline is implemented with per-channel weight quantization and per-token dynamic activation quantization plus FP16 mixed-precision decomposition for outlier channels as in Dettmers et al. 2022.
Code has been implemented that detects outlier activation channels using a magnitude threshold (default 6.0 following LLM.int8()) and routes those channels to an FP16 matmul path.

verification.spec: Feed a synthetic activation tensor containing known outlier channels (magnitudes > 6.0) through the LLM.int8() detector. Verify: (a) channels with any value > threshold=6.0 are identified as outlier channels, (b) those channels are routed to the FP16 matmul path (traced or via a counter), and (c) the threshold value 6.0 is configurable.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that performs per-channel INT8 weight quantization and per-token dynamic INT8 activation quantization on the non-outlier channels, then combines the INT8 and FP16 partial products to form the full linear-layer output.

verification.spec: Construct a linear layer with LLM.int8() decomposition. On a synthetic input with known outlier columns, verify: (a) non-outlier channels use per-channel INT8 weight scales and per-token dynamic INT8 activation scales, (b) outlier channels use FP16 matmul, (c) combined output matches within 1e-2 of an FP16 reference matmul on the same inputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The LLM.int8() baseline preserves OPT-175B accuracy at approximately the FP16 level as reported in Table 3 (~66.7% average across the 7 zero-shot tasks; WikiText PPL ~11.10).

verification.spec: Apply LLM.int8() (bitsandbytes) to OPT-175B and evaluate 7 zero-shot tasks with lm-eval-harness. Report average accuracy; expected ~66.7% (paper Table 3), close to FP16 66.9%.

sub_tasks.requirements: The LLM.int8() baseline exhibits the reported latency overhead relative to FP16 in the PyTorch context-stage benchmark of Figure 8 (typically slower than FP16 for OPT-13B/30B).

verification.spec: Benchmark PyTorch context-stage latency for OPT-13B batch=4 seq=512 in FP16 and with LLM.int8() on a single H100. After warmup, time 20 iterations each. Compute ratio latency(LLM.int8())/latency(FP16); paper Figure 8 reports ~371/296 ≈ 1.25 for OPT-13B seq 512 (LLM.int8 is slower).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Outlier Suppression baseline is implemented with per-tensor static weight and per-tensor static activation quantization as described in Wei et al. 2022 and Table 2.
Code has been implemented that applies the non-scaling LayerNorm reparameterization and token-wise activation clipping described in the Outlier Suppression paper prior to quantization.

verification.spec: Apply the Outlier Suppression preprocessing to a small transformer. Verify: (a) LayerNorm modules have had their affine parameters reparameterized/absorbed into the following linear (compare weights to a reference computation), and (b) token-wise activation clipping is applied at layer inputs using per-token thresholds computed from calibration, with clip magnitudes visible in the wrapped modules.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that calibrates per-tensor static INT8 scales for both weights and activations for the Outlier Suppression baseline using calibration samples.

verification.spec: Run the Outlier Suppression calibration on a small model with a small calibration set. Verify: (a) each weight tensor has one scalar INT8 scale, (b) each activation tensor has one scalar static INT8 scale stored (not recomputed at runtime), and (c) running inference twice on different inputs yields the same activation scale.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Outlier Suppression baseline fails on OPT-175B as reported in Table 3 (~36.0% average across the 7 zero-shot tasks; WikiText PPL ~96151).

verification.spec: Apply the Outlier Suppression baseline (per-tensor weight, per-tensor static activation quantization, calibrated on 512 Pile sentences) to OPT-175B and run zero-shot evaluation via lm-eval-harness on WinoGrande, HellaSwag, PIQA, LAMBADA, OpenBookQA, RTE, COPA plus WikiText perplexity. Compute the average accuracy over the 7 zero-shot tasks; verify it is approximately 36.0% (collapse) and WikiText PPL is on the order of 1e5 (~96151).

sub_tasks.requirements: All four baselines share a common evaluation harness and calibration protocol so that Table 3 / Table 4 comparisons against SmoothQuant are consistent.

Code has been implemented that exposes a single interface to swap between the four baseline quantizers (W8A8 naive, ZeroQuant, LLM.int8(), Outlier Suppression) and SmoothQuant O1/O2/O3 for a given LLM.

verification.spec: Import the quantization module and confirm that a single dispatch interface (e.g., a factory function or class taking a method-name argument) supports selecting among the seven schemes: W8A8-naive, ZeroQuant, LLM.int8(), Outlier-Suppression, SmoothQuant-O1, SmoothQuant-O2, SmoothQuant-O3. Instantiate each mode against a small dummy LLM (e.g., OPT-125M) and assert forward pass returns tensors of the expected shape.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that uses 512 random calibration sentences from the Pile validation set (shared with SmoothQuant) to calibrate the static baselines (naive per-tensor static, Outlier Suppression).

verification.spec: Run the calibration routine for a static baseline (e.g., Outlier Suppression) on a small OPT model. Verify that (1) exactly 512 sentences are sampled from the Pile validation split, (2) the sampling is shared with the SmoothQuant calibration path (same seed/loader), and (3) static per-tensor step sizes are produced and cached.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that applies each baseline to all linear layers (self-attention Q/K/V/O projections and FFN layers) and to the attention BMM operators wherever the baseline definition permits, matching the SmoothQuant quantization scope shown in Figure 6.

verification.spec: For each baseline, inspect a quantized OPT model and confirm that all self-attention Q/K/V/O projections and both FFN linear layers are wrapped with the baseline's quantized module, and that the two attention BMM operators are replaced with quantized BMM where the scheme supports it (SmoothQuant O1-O3, W8A8-naive). Enumerate modules by name and assert coverage.

sub_tasks.requirements: SmoothQuant O1/O2/O3 preserve FP16 accuracy on OPT-175B across the 7 zero-shot tasks and WikiText perplexity while baselines (W8A8, ZeroQuant, Outlier Suppression) collapse; LLM.int8() matches FP16 (Table 3).

Evaluation harness driver for OPT-175B under all methods (FP16 reference, W8A8, ZeroQuant, LLM.int8(), Outlier Suppression, SmoothQuant-O1/O2/O3) across the 7 zero-shot benchmarks and WikiText perplexity is implemented.

verification.spec: Load OPT-175B in FP16 via HuggingFace transformers and run lm-eval-harness on LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, OpenBookQA, RTE, COPA, plus WikiText perplexity. Confirm the harness completes and emits per-task metrics.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that applies each quantization method (W8A8 naive, ZeroQuant, LLM.int8(), Outlier Suppression, SmoothQuant-O1/O2/O3) to OPT-175B and produces an inference-ready quantized model with the schemes specified in Table 2.

verification.spec: For each of the 7 quantization methods, apply it to OPT-175B and verify that (a) the resulting model runs a forward pass end-to-end, (b) the weight/activation quantization schemes match Table 2 (weights and activations tensors have expected quantized dtypes/granularity at each linear layer).

sub_tasks.requirements: The evaluation driver runs each of the 8 methods (FP16 + 7 quantization variants) over each of the 8 benchmarks and dumps a table row per method with accuracy per task, an averaged accuracy over the 7 zero-shot tasks, and WikiText perplexity.

sub_tasks.requirements: Calibration for static-quantization methods (SmoothQuant-O3, Outlier Suppression) uses exactly 512 random sentences from the Pile pre-training dataset and produces a single set of smoothing factors / quantization step sizes reused across all downstream tasks.

Assert (1) exactly 512 sentences are drawn from the Pile dataset, (2) a single set of smoothing factors and static step sizes is produced, (3) the same cached factors are reused across multiple downstream benchmark evaluations (no re-calibration per task).

sub_tasks.requirements: SmoothQuant runs on OPT-175B use migration strength alpha=0.5 as specified in the paper.

verification.spec: Inspect the SmoothQuant config/call used for OPT-175B and assert that migration strength alpha == 0.5 exactly.

Code has been implemented and run to verify the quantization formula: quantization step size Delta = max(|X|) / (2^(N-1) - 1) with N=8 produces INT8 values in [-127,127] and X_bar = round(X/Delta) recovers X within Delta error

verification.spec: Implement symmetric INT8 quantizer per Eq.1; on random tensor X, compute Delta = X.abs().max() / 127; X_q = round(X/Delta).clamp(-127,127); X_dq = X_q * Delta; assert (X - X_dq).abs().max() <= Delta and X_q.abs().max() <= 127

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the SmoothQuant scaling transformation X_hat = X * diag(s)^-1, W_hat = diag(s) * W is mathematically equivalent to the original X*W (verified numerically to floating-point tolerance)

verification.spec: Given random X (T x Ci), W (Ci x Co), and s = max(|X_j|)^alpha / max(|W_j|)^(1-alpha) with alpha=0.5; compute Y1 = X @ W and Y2 = (X / s) @ (s[:,None] * W); assert torch.allclose(Y1, Y2, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the migration strength formula s_j = max(|X_j|)^alpha / max(|W_j|)^(1-alpha) is correctly implemented as specified in Equation 4

verification.spec: Instantiate the smoothing-factor function on synthetic X, W with known max-per-channel values; verify output equals max(|X_j|)^alpha / max(|W_j|)^(1-alpha) elementwise for several alpha in {0.0, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}

verification.paper_cite: Table 1, INT8 per-tensor row across OPT-13B/30B/66B

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the per-channel smoothing factor for Q/K/V projection inputs is fused into the preceding LayerNorm's weight (and bias) parameters offline, so no extra scaling op is needed at runtime before self-attention.

verification.spec: Instantiate a Transformer block; compute smoothing factor s from calibration activations at Q/K/V projection input; call fuse_ln_smoothing(layernorm, [q_proj, k_proj, v_proj], s); verify (1) layernorm.weight and layernorm.bias have been divided by s elementwise, (2) q/k/v_proj.weight has been multiplied by s along input dim, (3) forward pass output of the fused block matches the original block's output at the QKV projection outputs within 1e-3 relative error on a random input
verification.paper_cite: Section 4, 'we can easily fuse the smoothing factor into previous layers' parameters offline'

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the per-channel smoothing factor for FFN FC1 input is fused into the preceding LayerNorm's parameters offline.

verification.spec: For a Transformer block with post-attention LayerNorm feeding FC1: compute s from calibration activations at FC1 input; call fuse_ln_smoothing(post_attn_ln, [fc1], s); assert post_attn_ln.weight/bias divided by s, fc1.weight multiplied by s along input dim; forward pass of fused block matches original at FC1 output within 1e-3 relative error
verification.paper_cite: Section 4, Applying SmoothQuant to Transformer blocks / Figure 6

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the attention output projection (out_proj) and the FFN second linear (FC2) are quantized to INT8 weights and INT8 activations, in accordance with Figure 6's precision map.

verification.spec: Load a quantized SmoothQuant OPT model; iterate over transformer blocks; assert type(block.self_attn.out_proj) is W8A8Linear (or equivalent INT8 linear class) and type(block.fc2) is W8A8Linear; assert their weight tensors have dtype int8
verification.paper_cite: Figure 6, precision mapping for a Transformer block

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the Q*K^T and attn_probs*V batched matmuls in self-attention use INT8 BMM kernels.

verification.spec: Instantiate the SmoothQuant self-attention module; monkey-patch or introspect the bmm calls used for Q@K^T and attn@V; assert they dispatch to an INT8 BMM implementation (e.g., BMM_S8T_S8N_F32T from torch-int / CUTLASS) rather than torch.bmm on FP16 tensors. Run a forward pass with a random input and confirm no dtype-mismatch errors and output matches reference FP16 attention within 5% relative error.
verification.paper_cite: Figure 6; Section 4, 'We also quantize BMM operators in the attention computation'

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that LayerNorm, softmax, ReLU/GELU, and residual add operations remain in FP16 while only linear layers and attention BMMs are INT8.

verification.spec: Load a quantized SmoothQuant transformer block; hook every submodule's forward to record input/output dtypes on a sample forward; assert LayerNorm, softmax activation, GELU/ReLU, and residual add produce FP16 (torch.float16) tensors; assert linear layers and attention BMMs internally use int8 for weights/activations
verification.paper_cite: Section 4, 'keeping the activation as FP16 for other lightweight element-wise operations like ReLU, Softmax, and LayerNorm'

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that a smoothed-but-not-quantized transformer block (LayerNorm-fused smoothing applied, weights scaled) produces outputs equivalent to the original FP16 block within FP16 numerical tolerance on random inputs.

verification.spec: Take an OPT decoder block; make a deep copy; apply SmoothQuant smoothing (compute s from calibration data, fuse into preceding LayerNorm, scale linear weights) but keep all tensors in FP16 (no INT8 quantization); run both blocks on the same random FP16 input of shape (batch=2, seq=32, hidden); assert max_relative_error(orig_output, smoothed_output) <= 1e-2 (FP16 tolerance)
verification.paper_cite: Section 4, mathematically equivalent per-channel scaling transformation

Assert that for random input x, the fused module output matches the original module output within 1e-4 (mathematical equivalence). Repeat for the case where the preceding op is a nn.Linear rather than LayerNorm.
verification.paper_cite: Section 4, 'fuse the smoothing factor into previous layers' parameters offline'

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that adjusted weights W_hat = diag(s) @ W preserve numerical equivalence with the original linear layer

verification.spec: For random X of shape [T, C_in], W of shape [C_in, C_out], and random positive s of shape [C_in]: compute Y1 = X @ W; compute X_hat = X / s (broadcast on C_in), W_hat = s[:, None] * W, Y2 = X_hat @ W_hat. Assert torch.allclose(Y1, Y2, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4). Run for 5 random seeds.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that SmoothQuant smoothing is applied to the input activations of self-attention Q/K/V projections and to the FFN first linear (fc1) in each Transformer block

Verify end-to-end forward output on a fixed prompt matches the un-smoothed FP16 model within 1e-3 (equivalence).
verification.paper_cite: Section 4, 'Applying SmoothQuant to Transformer blocks'; Figure 6

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that BMM inputs in attention (Q, K, softmax(QK^T), V) are quantized to INT8 while LayerNorm, Softmax, and ReLU/GELU remain in FP16 per Figure 6

verification.spec: Import the SmoothQuant attention module; run a forward pass with a hook that records dtype at each operation boundary. Assert: (a) inputs to bmm(Q,K^T) are int8, (b) output of that bmm is dequantized to fp16 before softmax, (c) softmax runs in fp16, (d) inputs to bmm(attn_probs, V) are int8 (attn_probs re-quantized), (e) LayerNorm modules retain fp16 weight dtype. Fail if any of these five conditions is violated.
